newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says 1996 JV cash calls paid to June 30.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says 1996 JV cash calls paid to June 30.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has made 1996 cash call payments up to June 30 to foreign joint- venture partners in crude oil production, finance minister Anthony Ani said on Thursday.

"In respect of the 1996 Cash calls, provisions of $1.75 billion and 18 billion naira were made in the 1996 budget. Monthly payments .. have been made in accordance with these provisions and all cash calls up to and including June 1996 have been paid," Ani said in his half-yearly review of the annual budget.
Ani said 1995 cash calls had also been paid.

"As regards the pre-1995 cash calls arrears there was still an outstanding amount of $122.3 million and $300 million as at 31 December 1995. Arrangements have been made to liquidate these amounts on or before 15 November 1996," Ani said.
Ani said joint-venture partners had sought an increased budget in respect of both dollar and naira cash calls.
"The additional provisions, when agreed with the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation would be met by the government," he said.
It was not clear whether this meant the foreign companies were likely to receive their increased demands.
The five major joint-ventures are run by subsidiaries of Shell, Mobil, Chevron, Agip and Elf. State-run NNPC is the majority partner in all of them.
The OPEC producer pumps around two million barrels of crude oil per day.
